definition: Language models trained to follow instructions with human feedback; a precursor model to ChatGPT.
details: Language models trained to follow instructions with human feedback; a precursor model to ChatGPT.

explainer.lead: InstructGPT refers to language models trained to follow instructions using human feedback, and it is a precursor model to ChatGPT. It matters as an early step toward models that behave as instruction-following assistants rather than raw text predictors.

tiers.eli5: It is a version of a language model taught, with help from people rating answers, to do what you ask instead of just continuing your text.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat instruction-following training as the step that turns a base language model into a usable assistant. A pitfall is assuming such a model follows requests reliably in every domain; the behaviour comes from the training, not from the underlying pretraining alone.
tiers.paperLevel: InstructGPT is defined as language models trained to follow instructions with human feedback. Related background: GPT-3 is a decoder-only transformer with 175 billion parameters at 16-bit precision, a 2,048-token context window, and demonstrated zero-shot and few-shot learning.

explainer.example: A user asks the model to rewrite a paragraph in a formal tone, and the instruction-trained model produces the requested rewrite rather than simply continuing the text.
